summary: The note traces the history and practice of steam cooking, focusing on bamboo steamers in Asia from the Han Dynasty onward. It covers how the technique spread to Korea and Japan, how stacked bamboo layers are used, the foods suited to it such as dim sum, and its ritual role at festivals like the Mid-Autumn Festival. It closes with the modern resurgence of bamboo steaming, supported by quotes from several chefs and researchers.
one_line: A history and how-to of steam cooking, especially Asian bamboo steamers, covering spread, technique, foods, rituals and modern revival.
key_facts: Steam cooking dates back to prehistoric times and is one of the oldest methods of preparing food, originally using steam from boiling water with food suspended in baskets or on racks.
Records suggest bamboo steamers were in use during the Han Dynasty (206 BC – 220 AD).
Bamboo steamers are slatted baskets that stack, letting multiple dishes cook at once over a single heat source.
Bamboo is abundant in Asia, durable and sustainable, and imparts a subtle aroma to food.
Dr. Mei Lin of the Beijing Culinary Institute says bamboo absorbs excess moisture, which maintains the texture of dumplings and buns.
By the third century, evidence suggests Korea and Japan had adopted steam cooking.
Japan also used the mushiki, a wooden steamer, while Korea widely used the siru, an earthenware steamer.
In a bamboo steamer, the bottom layer holds items needing more steam such as fish or meats, while upper layers hold vegetables or delicate items.
Dim sum, a traditional brunch of steamed dumplings, buns and rolls served in bamboo baskets, is one of the most popular uses of bamboo steamers.
During the annual Mid-Autumn Festival, families in China prepare a feast with steamed delicacies symbolizing unity and prosperity.
Modern bamboo steamers can be used with electric and induction hobs.

Chef Taro Kuma spoke at a culinary workshop on September 5th, 2023; Chef Lily Hoang spoke at the International Steam Cookery Symposium on September 17th, 2023; Chef Anita Das spoke at a conference on September 30th, 2023.
